items.t: Nvidia says it’s investigating CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy
items.d: In a memo to the company, Huang admitted that he had an affair.
items.fullText: Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a Chinese spy operation . Bloomberg and other outlets reported that Huang sent a message to the company admitting that he had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. A memo circulated among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Jensen Huang wrote in his memo. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang added that he’d “fallen short’ of his responsibility to the company. “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said. AI chips, including those created by Nvidia, have been a major focus in the trade war between the United States and China . Huang also seems to have a close relationship with President Donald Trump . In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said that it has “no reason to believe” that either national security nor company secrets were compromised, and that Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.” The board also said it has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” The investigation will be conducted by independent directors working with outside legal counsel. In response to earlier reports about its CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair’s interactions were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with customers. Other companies involved in the AI boom have warned employees to be wary of possible spies , including those offering sex or romance. Topics AI , Government & Policy , Jensen Huang , nvidia Wh

(사진=로이터 연합뉴스) 세계 최대 파운드리(반도체 위탁생산) 기업 TSMC가 엔비디아 요청으로 차세대 '3차원(3D) D램' 생산을 검토 중이라는 외신 보도와 관련해 “기존 파운드리 사업에 집중한다”는 입장을 내놨다. 7일 미국 IT 매체 톰스하드웨어 등 현지 매체에 따르면 TSMC 대변인은 관련 질의에 “회사는 언제나 전업 반도체 위탁생산(파운드리)이라는 핵심 사업에 집중하고 있다”며 “앞으로도 글로벌 로직(비메모리) 반도체 산업에서 신뢰받는 기술·생산능력 공급자가 되는 것이 우리의 임무”라고 밝혔다. 대만 공상시보 역시 TSMC가 시장 소문이나 추측에 논평하지 않고 파운드리 본업에 집중한다는 원론적 입장을 고수했다고 전했다. 이번 진출설은 지난 6일(현지시간) 미국 정보기술(IT) 전문매체 디인포메이션 보도로 불거졌다. 이 매체는 TSMC가 엔비디아 요청을 받아 3D D램 생산 계획을 수립하기 시작했다고 전했다. 신규 팹(공장) 건설이나 기존 공장 인수·전환 방안이 거론됐으며, 구체적인 양산 시점은 알려지지 않았다. 첨단 패키징 부문을 이끄는 쉬궈진 7부사장이 프로젝트를 주도한다는 내용도 포함됐다. 보도 당시 TSMC와 엔비디아는 로이터의 논평 요청에 즉각 답하지 않았다. 대만 현지 업계에서는 신중론이 우세하다. 대만 경제일보에 따르면 자오유쥔 윈본드 회장은 “D램 사업을 영위하려면 독자 기술 확보와 복잡한 특허 문제 해결이 선행돼야 한다”고 지적했다. TSMC가 삼성전자·윈본드 등 메모리 기업과 첨단 패키징 분야에서 긴밀히 협력 중인 만큼, 자체 D램 개발 시 기존 파트너십과 내부 자원 배분 문제를 동시에 고려해야 한다는 설명이다. 진입 가능성 자체를 열어두는 시각도 있다. 류페이전 대만경제연구원 산업경제자료센터 책임자는 대만 중앙통신과 인터뷰에서 “기술 확장과 고객사 공급망 다변화 측면에서 진입 가능성을 완전히 배제할 순 없다”고 진단했다. 다만 막대한 투자 부담과 수익성, 메모리 협력사와의 관계를 감안하면 단기적으로는 표준 메모리 대량생산보다 공동개발이나 특정 기술 검증에 무게를 둘 것으로 내다봤다. 다만 이번에 거론된 3D D램은 한국 기업들의 주력 제품인 HBM과는 차이가 있다. 3D D램은 미세화 한계를 극복하기 위해 메모리 셀 자체를 수직으로 쌓는 차세대 기술로, 완성된 D램 칩 여러 개를 수직 적층하는 HBM과는 개념이 다르다. 반도체 업계 관계자는 “TSMC가 패키징과 로직 공정에서 역할을 넓히는 움직임을 곧바로 삼성전자·SK하이닉스와의 D램 직접 경쟁으로 연결 짓기는 어렵다”고 설명했다. 이형두 기자 dudu@etnews.com

items.t: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
items.d: A memo circulated earlier this year reportedly claimed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 1:17 PM PST · November 7, 2026 Image Credits: Benjamin Fanjoy / Getty Images Anthony Ha Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The New York Times, which had previously said Nvidia’s chief executive had been the target of Chinese intelligence, was the first to report on the memo . The Financial Times subsequently reported that the memo — supposedly based on U.S. intelligence — also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed. An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with its customers. A separate NYT report examined New Matrix, a Chinese company authorized by the U.S. Commerce Department to buy advanced Nvidia chips. But at the office address listed by New Matrix, reporters only found “a hollow gray shell,” raising concerns that it could be a front for a blacklisted private equity firm. Together, they give researchers a foundation for testing ideas, comparing results and building on each other’s work — connecting simulation and AI training with experiments on real over-the-air wireless systems. Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world. Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms. The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Create Editable 3D Assets With Houdini and AI Agents 🔗 Creating animated 3D content requires connecting modeling, simulation, materials and rendering. Nick Scarcella, a senior technical artist on NVIDIA’s BondLab team, directed AI agents — primarily using Claude — to work with CUDA libraries and Isaac Sim to create animations. The BondLab team uses SideFX Houdini and the NVIDIA ovrtx library to develop materials, lighting and the final rendered appearance. In one experiment, Scarcella guided Astra to recreate an OP-1 portable synthesizer using product images, manuals and technical direction. He exported the model into the OpenUSD framework, tested it in Houdini and Blender, then used Astra and Opus to refine details before adjusting materials and textures for ovrtx rendering. items.fullText: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models With a parakeet, a webcam and a conviction that AI belongs to everyone — how one NVIDIAN became NVIDIA Nemotron’s loudest advocate. November 5, 2026 by Matthew Leib 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Chris Alexiuk has a simple rule about open source AI: If you believe in it, be loud about it. “We should be shouting about this technology from the rooftops,” said Alexiuk, a Toronto-based senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in making open large language models (LLMs) practical for working developers. Alexiuk’s preferred “rooftop” is YouTube , where he’s built a following teaching curious thousands how to build, fine-tune, evaluate and ship production LLM applications and agents. “I think the people who will most help us understand how to build and apply AI likely haven’t even heard of it yet,” he said. “Trying to get knowledge and information out to as many people as humanly possible is what continues to drive me.” Bringing NVIDIA Nemotron to Developers Everywhere Having spent years teaching developers to build with open models, Alexiuk has concluded that transparency isn’t a feature of good AI; it’s the precondition for it. “Fully open source AI is necessary for the democratization of intelligence,” he said. “You should have access to the weights, the data that went into it, the training recipes, everything.” That’s why, on his LinkedIn profile, Alexiuk styles himself “No. 1 Nemotron Fan,” referring to the NVIDIA Nemotron family of open source, multimodal models built for long-running, self-evolving and specialized AI agents. “I think Nemotron is the most important project that exists,” said Alexiuk, who also uses the pseudonym “Joe Nemotron” across social media. “I’m a firm believer that openness is a very important thing to undertake, so I’m going to be the No. 1 fan of whoever is doing that the best. items.fullText: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge November 5, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack. But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory. That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit. How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed. Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it. From NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose roughly 3%, while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX. Agentic Inference Is Putting More Pressure on HBM Frontier models now have trillions of parameters — the values that hold what an AI model learned in training. KV cache, which holds the context the model needs to understand each active request without reprocessing the same information, is also expanding. AI 생태계를 조성한 엔비디아를 통해 국내 AI 스타트업의 해외 진출 길이 열릴지 주목된다. 5일 과학기술정보통신부에 따르면 오는 9일 서울 삼성동 코엑스에서 국내 AI 스타트업 최고경영자(CEO)와 엔비디아 주요 임원 간 비공개 간담회가 열린다. 지난 10월 리사 수 AMD CEO가 방한해 국내 AI 반도체 기업들과 협력 방안을 논의한 데 이어 두 번째다. 엔비디아에서는 젠슨 황 CEO의 장녀인 매디슨 황 수석이사를 포함해 디푸 탈라 로보틱스 및 에지 AI 부문 부사장과 조나단 코헨 응용 연구 부문 부사장 등이 참석한다. 국내에서는 AI 분야의 주요 스타트업이 참석할 예정이다. 리벨리온, 퓨리오사AI, 딥엑스 등 AI 반도체 기업과 업스테이지 등 AI 모델 개발사, 엘리스그룹 등 AI 인프라 기업이 참석 예정 및 검토 중인 것으로 알려졌다. 이번 행사는 엔비디아의 국내 행사 일정에 맞춰 과기정통부와 엔비디아가 국내 AI 스타트업과의 교류를 확대하기 위해 마련했다. 참석자들은 국내 AI 스타트업의 성장과 글로벌 시장 진출 방안, 기술 협력 가능성 등을 논의한다. 지난달 AMD와의 회동 이후 구체적인 성과가 가시화하고 있다. AMD는 국내 스타트업 망고부스트와 손잡고 AI 클라우드 인프라를 구축했으며, 국내 AI 반도체 기업들과 AMD의 중앙처리장치(CPU)·그래픽처리장치(GPU)를 결합한 컴퓨팅 인프라 실증도 추진하고 있다. 이번 엔비디아와의 만남에서도 국내 스타트업이 글로벌 AI 생태계에 참여하고 기술 상용화와 해외 고객사 확보 등으로 협력 범위를 넓힐 수 있을 것으로 기대된다. 과기정통부 관계자는 “간담회뿐 아니라 개별 기업과의 미팅도 논의 중이며, 구체적인 협력 방안은 현장에서 논의할 예정”이라고 말했다. 이영애 기자 0ae@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 이영애 ADVERTISEMENT 관련 뉴스 1 "너무 비싸게 샀나"…마벨, 루멘텀 인수발표 후 급락 한국경제신문의 투자 전문 유료 플랫폼 '한경 프리미엄9'에 실린 기사입니다. 한경 프리미엄9(www.hankyung.com/premium9)을 구독하시면 더 많은 글로벌 투자 기사를 찾아볼 수... 2026.11.03 17:54 2 제이 리터 "앤트로픽·오픈AI는 좋은 기업…하지만 좋은 주식은 아닐 수도" 한국경제신문의 투자 전문 유료 플랫폼 '한경 프리미엄9'에 실린 기사입니다. 한경 프리미엄9(www.hankyung.com/premium9)을 구독하시면 더 많은 글로벌 투자 기사를 찾아볼 수... 2026.11.02 18:03 3 '근원 경쟁력' 회복한 삼성…AI 전환·미래 투자 속도전 “오늘의 삼성을 넘어 진정한 초일류 기업을 만듭시다. 제가 그 앞에 서겠습니다.”이재용 삼성전자 회장이 회장직에 오른 2022년 10월 27일 삼성 사내 게시판에 ‘미래를 위한 도전&... 2026.10.25 18:34 ADVERTISEMENT 많이 본 뉴스 1 "2000원짜리에 또 난리났다"…다이소 갔더니 '품절입니다' 2026.11.04 19:28 2 150억에 회사 넘긴 노현정 남편…장례식장 647곳 손잡은 이유 2026.11.04 21:07 3 '진작 담아두길 잘했네' 개미들 환호…하루 만에 18% 터졌다 20

items.fullText: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI From infrastructure planning and transportation to public services, cities are using NVIDIA-powered applications to address local needs and expand capacity for the broader AI ecosystem. November 2, 2026 by Esther Lee 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge. Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used. Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own. Agentic AI for Cities From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. items.fullText: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories New AIOps platform connects infrastructure and workload telemetry to help operators increase uptime and maximize AI factory yield. October 22, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight. AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load. The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads. With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x. “Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. items.fullText: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck Companies around the world are using the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run AI factories as one system and unlock infrastructure development. October 21, 2026 by Vladimir Troy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues. One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together: NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground. NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability.
